# Your Version Number

> A bookmarkable web page that displays a person's "version number" — their age expressed as `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (decade.year-in-decade.days since their last birthday). Every view, including a card with a note, keeps all of its state in the URL; the site stores nothing. Inspired by [Jamie Thingelstad's 2018 post](https://www.thingelstad.com/2018/02/24/your-version-number.html) and Semantic Versioning.

The production site is static files served by Amazon S3 and CloudFront. No server-side code, no build step, no framework, vanilla JavaScript and CSS. Each "theme" is a standalone stylesheet contributors can add via pull request.

## Pages

- [Home](https://yourversionnumber.com/): the birthday product's front door. Asks your birthday, shows your number live, links into the birthday edition, the themes, the examples, the card composer and the about page. No URL state.
- [Work Edition front door](https://yourversionnumber.com/work/): the second product's own front door, in its own (deadpan office) voice, with its own themes, composer and about page under `/work/`. Old `/work/?j=` and `/work/?card=` links forward to the app.
- [Birthday Edition](https://yourversionnumber.com/birthday/): birthday-based version number. URL state: `?theme=<name>&p=Name:YYYY-MM-DD` (the `p` parameter is repeatable; the name is optional). Moved here from `/` in September 2026; old `/?p=...` bookmarks no longer resolve.
- [Work Edition](https://yourversionnumber.com/work/edition/): quarter-anchored version number for a job. `MAJOR` is years of tenure, `MINOR` is the quarter within the current tenure year (1–4, 3 calendar months apart from the anniversary), `PATCH` is business days into that quarter, and after the `+` a build number counts every business day ever logged (e.g. `3.2.40+888`). URL state: `?theme=<name>&j=Title:YYYY-MM-DD`. Moved from `/work/` in September 2026; `/work/` forwards those links.
- [Examples](https://yourversionnumber.com/examples/): eight worked examples, one to eight people, using public figures with well-documented birthdays. Each links into the birthday edition with the roster in the URL.
- [Theme gallery](https://yourversionnumber.com/themes/): live previews of the twenty birthday themes; enter a date and each preview renders your own number. The nine work themes have their own gallery at [/work/themes/](https://yourversionnumber.com/work/themes/). A theme belongs to one product; every stylesheet still renders if a URL names it in the other.
- [About](https://yourversionnumber.com/about/): the origin, the birthday and work arithmetic, and the privacy model (the URL is the only state).
- [Send a card](https://yourversionnumber.com/card/): builds a card link from a recipient name, birthday or work start date, theme, note, and sender name. The link is the card: `/birthday/?theme=<name>&card=Name:YYYY-MM-DD&from=Sender&note=Text` (or `/work/edition/?...` for a work anniversary, written by [/work/card/](https://yourversionnumber.com/work/card/)). `/card/new/` redirects here. Numbers use the viewer's local date; a countdown appears in the final seven days before the next occasion.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/jthingelstad/yourversionnumber.com)
- [README](https://github.com/jthingelstad/yourversionnumber.com/blob/main/README.md): URL format, theme list, deployment notes
- [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/jthingelstad/yourversionnumber.com/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): how to add a new theme

## Privacy

Every link contains everything it shows: names, dates, and theme, and on a card the note and sender. Nothing is stored server-side; there are no records, accounts, or expiry. Anyone holding a link can read it, forward it, or edit it. Links can be retained in browser history and sync. Use information you are comfortable sharing.

Tinylytics receives visit counts and interaction events. Query strings and fragments are removed from the page URL and referrer fields of analytics requests, so names, dates, and notes never reach it. Each edition stores one local flag to remember whether its intro has been shown; names, dates, themes, and card drafts are not saved in local storage.
